Quick update from infra triage (initial findings):
- Symptoms: sudden jump in 429s and increased tail latency for HealthSync starting 16:02 PDT, coincident with spike in retry attempts.
- Root cause (prelim): the org->project quota routing table contained a stale entry from an internal migration job (migration-20260415). ~40% of HealthSync's production tokens were incorrectly assigned to an older project-level quota (healthsync-legacy) that is on a lower tier. That meant HealthSync's high-volume traffic was hitting a much lower per-project cap and triggering 429s.
- Why it happened: migration-20260415 had an edge case where org tags with uppercase prefixes (HEALTHSYNC-ORG) were not normalized; the routing job created duplicate keys and wrote them to the per-project mapping instead of the org bucket.

Mitigations applied (16:35 — 16:45 PDT):
1) Emergency override: added a temporary org-cap override for HealthSync to the rate-limiter (manual patch) at 16:36. This reduced 429s to ~1.2% within ~6 minutes.
2) Circuit: enabled per-client circuit breaker for the HealthSync token group to reject aggressive retries for 60s windows (reduces retry storm amplification).
3) Rollback plan: reverting the migration mapping write (diff + rollback) and normalizing the tag parser.
4) Permanent fix: a migration job patch to normalize tags + unit tests + stale-key garbage collection scheduled.

Next steps / ask:
- Monica please keep the override in place until the migration fix is validated (we'll target 24h).
- CS team: confirm with HealthSync when their clients can ramp back retries.
- Engineering: create a postmortem and JIRA ticket for the migration job fix (I've created JIRA-2451).

I've attached the detection sample and a couple of request ids for deeper trace. Will follow with a short incident postmortem once we close the rollback.

— Marcus

- Client circuit-breaker throttles enabled to reduce retry amplification (Marcus/Marissa).
- Migration job rollback + normalization planned; JIRA-2451 opened.
